# Architecture

A tour of how Eddy fits together. For build/run, see
[`GETTING_STARTED.md`](GETTING_STARTED.md); for terms,
[`GLOSSARY.md`](GLOSSARY.md). The exhaustive in-repo reference (for LLM
collaborators) is [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md).

Eddy is three TypeScript apps on [Bun](https://bun.sh), plus a shared wire
package. Everything speaks one RPC framework end to end
([Connect-RPC](https://connectrpc.com) + protobuf).

```text
  Browser  (Solid SPA, any device on your tailnet)
     │
     │  Connect-RPC over HTTP/2, protobuf binary
     │    · unary            list calls, mutations
     │    · Sync stream      live deltas for 8 domains in one connection
     │    · inputStream      keystrokes (client-streaming)
     │    · scrollback       history, resumable from a byte offset
     ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Coordinator  (Bun · one Mac · :4102)        │
 │   append-only `events` table  (SQLite)      │
 │     → projected into a `sessions` table     │
 │   EdDSA-JWT auth · fans deltas to every tab │
 └────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                  │  raw WebSocket · protobuf frames · worker dials outbound
     ┌────────────┼────────────────────┐
     ▼            ▼                     ▼
  Worker       Worker                Worker     (Bun · one per Mac)
  Mac A        Mac B                 Mac C
     │  a keeper subprocess hosts every PTY over one UDS and
     │  outlives worker restarts; Claude Code's hooks
     │  track each agent's state
```

## The three apps

- **Web** (`apps/web/`) — a [Solid](https://www.solidjs.com) SPA on plain
  Vite. One `createStore` root; components read derived selectors and never
  mutate the store directly. URL is the source of truth for navigation. The
  terminal is `@wterm/dom`, a WASM VT core. Served as static files by the
  coordinator in production.
- **Coordinator** (`apps/coord/`) — `Bun.serve` with Connect-RPC, Kysely over
  `bun:sqlite`. It is control-plane only: auth, the append-only event log, the
  `sessions` projection, and fan-out to browsers. It never holds PTY state of
  its own.
- **Worker** (`apps/worker/`) — runs once per Mac, purely outbound. It dials
  the coordinator, owns the PTYs (via a single multiplexed keeper subprocess),
  runs a per-channel state machine, and turns Claude Code's hooks into agent
  events. There is no inbound port on a worker.
- **Shared** (`apps/shared/`) — the wire source of truth: protobuf definitions,
  generated TS, Zod schemas, and the `foldEvent` reducer (below).

## Event sourcing is the spine

A session's state is never sent as a snapshot that can drift. The worker emits
small `SessionEvent`s (opened, attached, cwd changed, agent state changed,
closed). The coordinator appends each to the `events` table and folds it into
the `sessions` projection inside one SQLite transaction. The browser folds the
same events into its Solid store.

Both sides fold with the **same** `foldEvent` function from `@eddy/shared`. So
the server's projection and the browser's view agree by construction, not by
careful hand-mirroring. A reconnecting browser sends the last event id it saw
and gets exactly the events it missed.

## Two hot paths

**A. Terminal bytes (keystroke → screen).** The browser streams keystrokes up a
single long-lived `inputStream` RPC. The coordinator forwards them over the
worker's WebSocket; the worker writes them into the keeper, which writes the
PTY. Output flows back the same way and rides the `Sync` stream's bytes channel
out to every browser watching that session.

**B. Agent state (Claude turn → sidebar).** Claude Code fires hooks as it works.
The worker turns those into `agent` `SessionEvent`s, which travel up as
proto frames, get appended + projected by the coordinator, and reach the SPA on
the `Sync` stream. The sidebar chip (working / needs-input / idle, plus model
and cost) is a selector over that projected state.

## Terminal fidelity (the hard part)

Streaming raw bytes to a browser terminal looks simple and corrupts in
practice: every window resize re-reflows history at a new width, and reconnects
duplicate or drop output. After a long fight with that corruption, Eddy moved to
the model mosh and tmux use:

- The **worker** holds the one authoritative grid per session and rebuilds it at
  a single agreed width on resize.
- The **browser** renders that grid as-is and never re-reflows it.
- History is **resumable**: every byte carries a monotonic sequence number, so a
  client asks for "everything since seq N" and the stream splices back with no
  gap and no duplication.

This is the part of the codebase with the most scar tissue; the recurring
failure modes and their fixes are catalogued in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Resilience

- **Worker loses the coordinator** — it reconnects with backoff (500 ms → 30 s);
  PTYs keep running in the keeper; on reconnect it emits a snapshot to
  reconcile.
- **Worker process crashes** — the keeper is a separate process, so PTYs
  survive; the restarted worker reattaches over the UDS and re-adopts open
  sessions.
- **Browser disconnects** — the `Sync` stream reconnects and backfills from the
  last event id; scrollback re-fetches from the last byte offset.
- **Coordinator restarts** — workers redial, browsers reconnect, and every
  session is re-projected from the event log. No state is lost because the log
  is the source of truth.

## Entry points

- **Web:** `apps/web/src/main.tsx` (mount) · `routes.ts` ·
  `store/{root,projector,sync,selectors}.ts` · `connect.ts` (RPC client) ·
  `components/CellTerminal.tsx` · `ws/input-channel.ts`
- **Coordinator:** `apps/coord/src/main.ts` (Bun wrapper) ·
  `coord-factory.ts` (`createCoord`) · `connect/router.ts` +
  `connect/handlers-*.ts` · `connect/auth-interceptor.ts` · `event-log.ts` ·
  `buses.ts` · `db/`
- **Worker:** `apps/worker/src/main.ts` · `session-manager.ts` ·
  `transport/CoordLink.ts` · `keeper/multiplexed-main.ts` · `claude/hooks.ts` ·
  `detect/` (agent screen-scrape) · `fsm.ts`
- **Shared:** `apps/shared/proto/eddy/v1/*.proto` · `src/wire/event.ts`
  (`foldEvent`)

I'm identifying the test files I'll need to extend—the attachment upload tests and the transfers store tests—and confirming that adding the hasher field to InFlight is backward compatible. Now I'm ready to outline the full scope of this cross-cutting change.

The implementation spans five layers: proto definitions for the new FilesReadChunk and AttachmentProbe RPCs, wire protocol frames for those operations, worker-side handlers for reading file chunks and probing attachments plus the manifest tracking logic, coordinator handlers to bridge those operations, and the web layer with a new transfers store replacing the old uploads system, format utilities for speed and ETA display, a new TransferCard component, and integration points throughout the app to wire everything together.

For the build order, I need to start with proto regeneration so the types are available, then add the wire frames as additive union members before the worker handlers can use them, then implement the worker handlers and manifest logic, and finally the coordinator handlers which depend on both the proto types and wire frames. Adding proto messages... Writing the coordinator handler... Defining the attachment-probe control frame schema... Writing attachment probe handler... Writing manifest functions... For the manifest file, I should define `MANIFEST_NAME` in attachment-reaper.ts alongside the other utility functions, then import it into attachment-upload.ts—this keeps the reaper logic self-contained and lets the list-attachments handler use the same import path it already has.

I need to update the list-attachments loop to skip the manifest file, checking whatever exclusion logic already exists there and adding the manifest name to it if needed.

Now moving on to the web download chunking...

Writing download handler... Finishing the error handler and then moving on to the smoke test additions for the download worker, including a function that runs the chunked file read loop and returns the byte count and SHA256 hash.

For the attachment probing, I'm adding a passthrough to `attachmentProbe` that calls the coordinator client, then combining it with the existing upload to create a dedup check — upload synthetic bytes, compute their hash, probe for a hit, and verify the path matches the first upload.

Now I'm setting up the e2e test flow: spawn a worker, upload a 30 MB file in chunks, probe for dedup with the hash and size, then read the file back in chunks to reassemble and verify the byte count matches.

For the upload, I need to generate deterministic test bytes (each byte set to its index modulo 256) so the worker's hash computation matches what the test calculates using Bun's crypto hasher.

For the non-gated unit tests, I'm extending the attachment-upload test to verify the full flow: after chunking data into a temp directory, probe the attachment by sha256 and confirm the saved path matches, then test that overwriting prunes the old hash entry, and finally verify the probe fails after unlinking the file. I need to check how the existing test configures the home directory and attachment base path so I can point it to a temp location.

For the store tests, I'm adding transfer progress tracking with deterministic speed and ETA calculations. Since the speed computation relies on `performance.now()`, I'll either inject a clock or make the timestamp injectable as a parameter to `setTransferProgress` — the injectable approach is cleaner for testing since it lets me control the timing without monkeypatching.

Now I'm structuring the plan document with sections for context, the six-step approach (wire contract, worker chunked read, coordinator relay, web store and M3 card, download and upload wiring, cleanup), critical file anchors, verification steps, and assumptions.

I need to clarify that the deletion of the old upload UI isn't housekeeping—it's part of the feature cutover, so I'll integrate those deletions into steps 5 and 6 rather than treating them as separate cleanup.

Before I write it out, I'm double-checking the Material Web linear-progress element: it takes a `value` between 0 and 1, an `indeterminate` boolean flag, and an optional `buffer` attribute. I'll wire that up in the Solid component with the percentage and indeterminate state based on whether we're hashing or the total is zero.

For the property binding, I need to use `prop:value` and `prop:indeterminate` to ensure Solid sets the actual properties rather than attributes, since Material Web components rely on property access. I'll also add the side-effect import of the linear-progress element in TransferCard.tsx and update the type definitions.

Now I'm looking at the color tokens available in theme-vars.css. I'll use `--md-sys-color-primary` for the progress fill, `--color-ok` for completed transfers, and `--color-err` for errors. The direction distinction will come from the up/down glyphs and accent text rather than different fill colors, keeping the design simple.

I need to add `"filesReadChunk"` and `"attachmentProbe"` to the `AttachmentMethods` type union in handlers-attachments.ts. Since the router spreads `makeAttachmentHandlers` into the service literal, including these two new methods in the handler file ensures the ServiceImpl type stays complete without needing changes to router.ts. The generated SessionsService and CoordinatorService types will automatically include the new RPCs. The browser sends offset as a BigInt, which proto-es converts to bigint, but the coordinator needs to convert it back to a number for the filesystem read since it's safe under JavaScript's number limit. Similarly, the response size comes back as bigint from proto-es, and I'll convert that to a number for the total. Now I'll write this out.
I now have a complete, grounded picture across all layers. Writing the plan.

I've also specified the mount swap, deletion commands with grep, and all the tests and verification steps needed. I've grounded every anchor by reading the actual files, and for the one thing that needs runtime confirmation—the md-linear-progress import path—I've got a concrete fallback ready.

Now I'm wrapping this up with a resolve call using apply, keeping the title aligned with the slug.

Plan written to `local://transfer-ui-plan.md` — decision-complete and fully grounded (every path, signature, field number, and anchor came from files I read this session).

**Summary of what it specifies:**

- **Download → chunked.** New `FilesReadChunk` RPC (byte-range read on the worker, no 25 MB cap) mirroring the proven upload relay path, so the browser sees bytes arrive → real progress/speed/ETA.
- **One unified M3 card** (`TransferCard.tsx`, real `md-linear-progress`) replaces both the upload chip *and* the download toast — filename, bar, bytes/total, %, **speed**, **time-left**, for both directions. Superseded `AttachmentChip.tsx` + `uploads.ts` deleted (clean cutover).
- **Content dedup.** Client SHA-256 (≤64 MiB) → new `AttachmentProbe` RPC → worker checks a per-session hash→path manifest (worker hashes incrementally during assembly via `Bun.CryptoHasher`). Hit = skip the byte transfer, reuse the path. **By content, never by name** — prune-by-value keeps a returned path honest after same-name/different-content overwrites.

★ **Key design calls I made (override points, all in the plan's Assumptions):**
- **Chunked-unary over server-streaming** for download — reuses the exact `createPendingRpc`/`sendBrowserCmd` pattern upload already uses; lowest risk, matches the codebase's "connect-web can't stream requests, chunk it" precedent.
- **Worker self-hashes** during assembly → no change to `AttachFileChunkRequest`/`DAttachmentChunk` wire frames; only a probe RPC is added. Smaller blast radius.
- **Per-session dedup + 64 MiB client-hash cap** — the pragmatic scope; larger scopes (cross-session, huge-file dedup, streamed-to-disk downloads) are named with concrete fallbacks rather than left open.

Verification is layered: `proto:gen` + typecheck, deterministic units (speed/ETA math, dedup manifest), a gated live-coord e2e proving a 30 MB round-trip + dedup hit, and a manual visual check.

blocks.text:
## Goal
Improve upload AND download UX in the Eddy web app so both:
1. Use proper Material Design 3 (M3) elements, consistent between the two flows.
2. Clearly surface transfer **speed**, **bytes/time remaining (ETA)**, and **progress**.
3. Receive the same treatment (user: "it should be the same for upload").

This is a **plan-mode** session; the destination plan file is `local://transfer-ui-plan.md` (executor MUST read it directly after compaction — it is the authoritative spec). NOTE: in the visible history the plan file was not yet written; exploration was still finishing.

## Constraints & Preferences
- App = Eddy: Solid SPA (`apps/web/`) on Vite, Material 3; three Bun apps (web / coordinator :4102 / worker) speaking Connect-RPC + protobuf. Coord↔worker is raw WebSocket protobuf frames.
- Solid store rule: components read derived selectors, never mutate store directly.
- Upload and download must look/behave consistently.

## Progress

### Done (exploration)
- [x] Mapped **upload flow**: chunked-unary `attachFileChunk` RPC, 4 MiB chunks (`CHUNK_BYTES` in `apps/web/src/lib/attachments.ts`), serial Promise-chain queue. `uploadAttachment(session, file, onProgress)` fires `onProgress(bytesSent)` after each acked chunk; `enqueueAttachment` shows an M3 `md-input-chip` progress chip (`AttachmentChip.tsx`, state in `store/uploads.ts`) with name + bytes sent/total + % + progress bar. "ok" chips auto-dismiss 2s, "err" stay.
- [x] Mapped **download flow**: unary `filesRead` RPC returns the WHOLE file at once → no incremental progress possible today. `downloadWorkerFileByHref(href)` in `apps/web/src/lib/downloadWorkerFile.ts` only shows a persistent toast `Downloading {name}…` (`addToast(..., { ttlMs: null })`). `parseFileHref` decodes `/file/<workerFp>/<enc path>[#L<n>]`; wired to CellTerminal Cmd/Ctrl-click.
- [x] Proto (`apps/shared/proto/eddy/v1/coordinator.proto`): L410 `FilesReadRequest { worker_fp=1; path=2 }`, L411 `FilesReadResponse { bytes data=1; uint64 size=2 }`, L559 `rpc FilesRead`. Coord handler `filesRead` in `apps/coord/src/connect/handlers-attachments.ts` forwards a browser-cmd frame via `sendBrowserCmd`/`createPendingRpc`; `attachFileChunk` handler relays raw chunks to the worker.
- [x] Helpers found: `formatBytes(n)` in `apps/web/src/lib/format.ts`; `addToast` returns a `dismiss()` fn (`toastStore.ts`).

### In Progress
- [ ] grep for the worker-side file read handler (`filesRead|readFile|attachFileChunk`) in `apps/worker/src` — **SKIPPED because a user message was queued**; must retry after handling that message.
- [ ] Plan direction chosen but plan file `local://transfer-ui-plan.md` not yet written.

### Blocked
- A **queued user message** was pending at end of session (interrupted the worker grep). Its content is not visible — handle it before resuming.

## Key Decisions
- **Download needs an RPC change, not just UI**: because `FilesRead` is unary/whole-file, real speed/ETA/progress is impossible without chunking. Leaning toward **Scope B — add a chunked-unary `filesReadChunk` RPC** mirroring upload's `attachFileChunk` (request: worker_fp, path, offset, length; response: chunk bytes + total size + EOF flag). Browser drives the loop and computes speed/ETA. Uses existing connect-web chunked-unary capability (no server-streaming needed); server-streaming exists in-stack but was not chosen.
- **Rejected — Scope A (UI-only, keep unary download)**: cannot show real progress → fails the explicit user requirement.
- **Upload speed/ETA is easy**: derive from elapsed time inside the existing `onProgress` callback; no protocol change.
- **Unify presentation**: both flows should share one M3 progress component (extend the existing `md-input-chip` chip pattern rather than the plain download toast).

## Next Steps
1. Handle the pending **queued user message** first.
2. Retry the skipped grep for the worker file read handler in `apps/worker/src`; confirm the worker can do byte-range reads (slice offset→offset+length) to back `filesReadChunk`.
3. Confirm coord relay path for a chunked download (mirror `attachFileChunk` relay in `handlers-attachments.ts`).
4. Decide/confirm the shared M3 progress UI (extend `AttachmentChip`/`uploads.ts` store to also represent downloads, or a shared component) showing name, %, bytes sent/total, **speed**, **ETA**.
5. Write the full spec to `local://transfer-ui-plan.md`, then `resolve` with `action: "apply"`, `extra: { title: "transfer-ui" }`.

## Critical Context
- Executor MUST open `local://transfer-ui-plan.md` after compaction — canonical source of truth.
- Key files: `apps/web/src/lib/downloadWorkerFile.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/attachments.ts`, `apps/web/src/components/AttachmentChip.tsx`, `apps/web/src/store/uploads.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/format.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/toastStore.ts`, `apps/shared/proto/eddy/v1/coordinator.proto` (L410-411, L559), `apps/coord/src/connect/handlers-attachments.ts`, plus worker handler (TBD in `apps/worker/src`).
- Plan-mode rules: read-only tree; no writes except `local://` artifacts; leave only via `ask` or `resolve`.

## Additional Notes
The download unary→chunked change spans proto + generated code + worker + coord + web; upload changes are web-only. Any new `filesReadChunk` message/RPC field names and the worker byte-range read remain to be verified before the plan is decision-complete.

---

**Turn Context (split turn):**

## Original Request

The user asked for upload **deduplication by content checksum** (not filename): when the same file content is uploaded twice, the system should detect it via hash, skip the redundant upload, and return the existing path. The assistant expanded scope to also include: **chunked download with progress tracking** (speed + ETA) and a **unified transfer UI** for both uploads and downloads.

## Early Progress

**Codebase**: Eddy v2 monorepo (Bun + TS + Solid, `apps/*` workspaces). Proto codegen via `cd apps/shared && buf generate` (script `proto:gen`), output to `src/gen/eddy/v1/`.

**Download path (current)**: Browser `downloadWorkerFileByHref` → `coordClient.filesRead` → coord `filesRead` (in `apps/coord/src/connect/handlers-attachments.ts` L33) sends `read-file` cmd via `sendBrowserCmd`/`createPendingRpc` → worker `readFileRpc` (`apps/worker/src/file-rpcs.ts` L19). **Unary, base64, 25 MB ceiling** (`READ_FILE_MAX_BYTES = 25*1024*1024`, L12). Worker comment says "Bigger → chunk it (see AttachFileChunk)". **Decision**: add chunked-unary `read-file-chunk` cmd (path, offset, length → base64 data, total size, EOF flag), mirroring existing pattern; removes size cap.

**Upload path (current)**: Browser chunks 4 MiB → `coordClient.attachFileChunk` → worker `handleAttachmentChunk` (`apps/worker/src/attachment-upload.ts` L55) appends to temp file `~/.eddy/attachments/<session_id>/.upload-<request_id>`, renames on `last` chunk via `uniqueName(dir, sanitizeAttachmentName(...))`, replies `abs_path` (or `linkShortPath(dir,fpath)` if `shortPath`). Memory O(chunk). `InFlight` interface (L40): `{tmpPath, fd, filename, shortPath, dir, bytesWritten, nextSeq, lastChunkMs}`. Chunks carry 0-based `seq`; seq≠0 with no state = REFUSE.

**Reaper** (`apps/worker/src/attachment-reaper.ts`): sweeps hourly, 24h TTL, 1 GB LRU cap. Helpers: `attachmentBaseDir()`, `attachmentSessionDir()`, `resolveSessionDirWithinBase()` (path-traversal guard), `sanitizeAttachmentName()` (L103). Sweep loop L47-99 does `fs.readdirSync` per session dir.

**Dedup design decided**:
- Client-side SHA-256 for files **≤ 64 MiB** (threshold tunable); larger files skip probe/dedup. Browser SHA-256 pattern exists at `apps/web/src/auth/web-key.ts` L120-124 (`crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256",...)` → hex).
- New `attachmentProbe` RPC: browser sends hash+size before uploading; coord relays to worker (resolve worker_fp via session lookup like `attachFileChunk`); worker checks per-session JSON manifest; hit + file exists → return existing path (honor `short_path`), skip transfer; miss → normal upload.
- Worker self-hashes during assembly via `Bun.CryptoHasher` (sync update/digest per chunk in `InFlight`), records hash→filename in `.eddy-manifest.json` in session dir on save.
- **Prune-on-write**:

<advisory severity="nit" guidance="weigh, don't blindly obey">
Verification gap: the core new download path — `readFileChunkRpc` offset/eof math — is only exercised by the EDDY_API_SMOKE-gated e2e (may never run in CI). Add a cheap always-on worker unit test: write a temp file, read via `readFileChunkRpc` in 2+ chunks, assert reassembled bytes match and `eof` fires correctly for the exact-multiple, partial-tail, and empty-file (size 0) cases. That's where off-by-one bugs in chunked readers live.
</advisory>
